items.prompt: When can fee(a+b,r)=fee(a,r)+fee(b,r) be a wrong test requirement?

options.text: Whenever the code is written in Python instead of C++
options.why: The language alone does not change the contractual identity.

options.text: Whenever the result is stored as integer cents
options.why: Exact integer multiplication does satisfy this identity.

options.text: Whenever a test contains more than one assertion
options.why: Assertion count is unrelated to whether the property is valid.

options.text: When the fee policy has tiers or per-trade rounding
options.why: Those policies can make split and combined fees differ.

items.explanation: A test must reflect the model. Tier thresholds or rounding on each trade can break simple additivity, so the contract must decide.
